# Palamedes

> Palamedes is open-source i18n tooling for TypeScript applications, with familiar macro-style authoring, repository-owned source-string-first catalogs, a native toolchain for the full local workflow, one runtime model, and first-party integrations for supported hosts.

Use this file when an AI coding assistant needs a compact overview of Palamedes. For a larger context bundle, use `/llms-full.txt`.

## Setup and migration skill

The repository-owned `skills/palamedes/SKILL.md` routes agent-assisted setup and
verification for Next.js 16 App Router on Node and Vite/React browser apps, plus
Lingui-to-Palamedes migration. See [/docs/agent-skill.md](/docs/agent-skill.md).
Its recipes require a target with the compiled v2 adapter contract; check
installed capabilities and matching release docs rather than assuming registry
`latest` supports the current repository. Preserve locale policy and map old
IDs to source text plus context in every locale before extraction or removal.

## Core rules for agents

- Prefer Palamedes' own packages and docs over Lingui, i18next, next-intl, or react-intl patterns.
- Treat `message + context` as the public translation identity.
- Do not invent explicit message IDs. Palamedes intentionally avoids explicit-ID sprawl.
- Do not introduce numeric placeholder fallbacks as an authoring strategy. Prefer stable named variables and clear markup.
- Use `getI18n()` as the public runtime access model when transformed code needs the active instance.
- Keep framework adapters thin; host-specific packages should wire Palamedes, not duplicate catalog semantics.
- Treat the framework matrix as verification of the shared model, not as an assumption that one application uses every supported framework.
- Use `.po` catalogs through Palamedes/ferrocat semantics. FCL is an opt-in catalog format for canonical, merge-friendly generated catalogs.
- The native core builds on three first-party Rust crates: `ferrocat` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferrocat) for catalog and ICU semantics, `ferromark` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferromark) for CommonMark and MDX parsing behind the MDX extraction path, and `ferralk` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferralk) for parallel source traversal during extraction. Ferralk's walker-dialect PatternSet also owns native CLI include/exclude matching in extraction and watch mode; patterns use `/` separators on every platform. Report issues in those areas against the crate that owns them.
- Palamedes+ is a planned optional managed layer for translation automation and collaboration. Palamedes itself covers the full local open-source workflow and does not require an account.
- Prefer `pmds audit` for catalog QA and `pmds report --fail-if-below <percent>` for completeness gates in CI.
- Advisory CLI update checks shipped in 1.24.0; 1.25.0 has documented publication evidence for all six CLI platforms. Service readiness is complete; only the released-client Rybbit observation remains pending in Palamedes #1036 and version-service #12. All six release CLI builds embed exactly `https://version-service.sebastian-software.de/check`; invalid values fail the build, ordinary builds without the endpoint stay disabled, and packaging smoke checks opt out. When enabled, checks are limited to one attempt per 24 hours, send only project/version/OS/architecture/CI plus a year-month install cohort, respect `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and `PALAMEDES_UPDATE_CHECK=0` before cache/network access, and print notices only on stderr. Coarse dimensions do not guarantee anonymity or prevent every linkable combination. The shared service (sebastian-software/version-service) reads path, `Content-Type`, and `Content-Length` only for protocol validation and forwards nothing but the documented aggregate dimensions to its sink; application code does not access or persist client IP, forwarded, user-agent, or other identifying headers. Request volume is not a unique-installation or active-user count. The existing oss-metrics public snapshot has no Rybbit source yet; a future integration must expose aggregate checks with explicit windows, freshness, and source status, keep credentials/raw events private, and avoid treating missing data as zero. See `/docs/cli.md` and `/adr/016-privacy-bounded-cli-update-check.md` for rollout evidence, service limitations, and disable/rollback ownership.
- Configure through `palamedes.yaml` (or `.yml`/`.json`/`.toml`). The native `pmds` CLI does not read JavaScript or TypeScript config files.
- Most published packages require Node.js `>=22.0.0`; `@palamedes/waku`, `@palamedes/tanstack`, and `@palamedes/react-router-rsc` require `>=22.22.0`, while `@palamedes/remix` requires `>=24.3.0`. Repository development and CI require `>=22.22.0`.
- Palamedes v2 package roots and `compiled` aliases share one parser-free runtime. Catalog entries must be compiled before use. Missing entries and execution failures throw; `onMissing` and `onError` observe failures, and `keepSourceFallbacks` only retains diagnostic metadata. Set `keepSourceFallbacks: false` for compact output. Standard adapters provide adapter-owned active-locale catalog delivery, shared server catalog storage and ordinary host error UI; applications do not build catalog maps or serialized ICU transport. See `docs/migration-v2.md`.
- Next.js advanced adapter options include `messageSplitting: true`, `serverFunctions: true`, `palamedes.server`, and `initializeServerFunctionI18n`.
- Next.js locale negotiation is read-only: do not renew locale cookies in Server Function initializers or on every middleware/proxy action POST. Persist explicit choices separately and skip unchanged writes; application data mutations own revalidation.
- Before adding the native CLI or a native-backed integration, check `/docs/platform-support.md` for the six published targets, unsupported Node processes, and recovery steps.
- Remix targets stable `remix@^3.0.0` and uses `remix/component` runtime and JSX paths. RC.1 is unsupported. Set `data-palamedes-time-zone` on `<html>` and the same server `createI18n` time zone for matching date/time output during hydration.
- Today, start with scoped packages such as `@palamedes/vite-plugin`, `@palamedes/next-plugin`, `@palamedes/waku`, `@palamedes/tanstack`, `@palamedes/cli`, `@palamedes/core`, `@palamedes/react`, `@palamedes/solid`, `@palamedes/remix`, and `@palamedes/runtime`. `@palamedes/react-router-rsc` is opt-in experimental support for the exact tested React Router RSC Framework Mode versions.
- TanStack Start: React examples pin Start 1.169.4 and Router 1.170.46. Solid is verified separately with Solid 2 Start Mode/Nitro. Both demo families are executable integration tests; TanStack Solid Start is outside the v2 scope and has no adapter export.
- Browser language preferences match configured locales case-insensitively and infer script/region with `Intl.Locale.maximize()`; cookie and route identities stay exact. See `/docs/locale-strategies.md`.
- Prerendered sites can use the headless `suggest()` and choice-handoff helpers from `@palamedes/core/locale`; applications own suggestion UI, and locale detection alone does not write cookies or redirect.
- Do not recommend the reserved top-level `palamedes` or `create-palamedes` packages as the main install path yet.
- The reserved `palamedes` and `create-palamedes` bins do not perform work: both print `https://palamedes.dev/docs/first-working-translation` to stderr, exit 1 when invoked without arguments, and exit 2 when arguments are supplied.
- Waku is Preview, verified with Waku 1.0.0-rc.3 and React/React DOM/react-server-dom-webpack 19.3.1. Upstream RC maturity and the unreleased v2 publication preview are separate from this SemVer tier: required unstable_getRequest and host CSP unstable_setNonce APIs must gain stable equivalents and pass regression proofs before promotion. See `/docs/stability.md#waku-preview-contract`.

## Install patterns

### Vite + React

```bash
pnpm add @palamedes/core @palamedes/react @palamedes/runtime @palamedes/vite-plugin
pnpm add -D @palamedes/cli @vitejs/plugin-react vite typescript
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react"
import { palamedes } from "@palamedes/vite-plugin"

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [palamedes(), react()],
})
```

### Vite + Solid

```bash
pnpm add @palamedes/core @palamedes/solid @palamedes/runtime @palamedes/vite-plugin @solidjs/web solid-js
pnpm add -D @palamedes/cli @solidjs/vite-plugin vite typescript
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import solid from "@solidjs/vite-plugin"
import { palamedes } from "@palamedes/vite-plugin"

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [palamedes({ framework: "solid" }), solid({ extensions: [".mdx"] })],
})
```

## Minimal config

```yaml
# palamedes.yaml
locales: [en, de]
source-locale: en
catalogs:
  - path: src/locales/{locale}
    include: [src]
```

The native `pmds` CLI discovers `palamedes.yaml`, `palamedes.yml`, `palamedes.json`, or `palamedes.toml`. Legacy `palamedes.config.ts`/`.js` files are a compatibility path read only by the JS plugin loaders via `@palamedes/config` — do not generate them for new projects.

## Minimal runtime

The standard Vite adapter owns the client runtime and catalog delivery. Do not
create an app-owned `i18n` module, import locale catalogs, or call `load()` and
`activate()` from application code. The adapter derives the translated module's
compiled active-locale dependency and awaits it before the module runs. Set the
document's `lang` before the module entry, for example `<html lang="de">`.

Package roots and `compiled` aliases share one parser-free runtime in v2. Raw ICU
source is compiled before use; application-owned catalog maps and serialized ICU
transport are not part of the standard framework flow.

## Minimal translated code

```tsx
import { Trans } from "@palamedes/react/macro"

export function App() {
  return (
    <h1>
      <Trans>Welcome to Palamedes</Trans>
    </h1>
  )
}
```

Then run:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds extract
pnpm exec pmds audit
pnpm exec pmds report
```

## Catalog workflow commands

`pmds` loads external en/de/es/fr UI catalogs, including English, from adjacent
`pmds-locales/` files or `PALAMEDES_UI_CATALOG_DIR`. No language is embedded.
`PALAMEDES_UI_LOCALE` overrides
`LC_ALL > LC_MESSAGES > LANG`; unsupported/invalid/C/POSIX values fall back to
English. UI language does not change catalog `--locale` selection, JSON, codes,
or exit statuses. Technical diagnostics and plugin messages keep their wording.
Missing or incompatible UI catalogs fail explicitly. Experimental Rust workspace
crates `palamedes-build` and `palamedes-i18n` provide Cargo generation and a
parser-free external catalog runtime. Cardinal/ordinal plurals use ICU4X/CLDR
rules with exact branches, offsets, and scoped `#` (plain decimal output).
Generated plural/ordinal calls require built-in numeric types or a validated
`PluralNumber`; bare strings fail compilation. Parse decimal strings into
`PluralNumber` to preserve visible fractional zeros.
Number/date/time formatting remains unsupported. Format version 2 requires
matching regenerated catalogs and schemas; see `docs/rust-applications.md`.
The Preview Rust SDK stays in the coordinated version set and is not published on crates.io. `pnpm verify:rust-sdk` checks actual Cargo archives, rustdoc, a staged-registry version-only consumer, and an unchanged binary after a native CLI translation update. `pnpm release:rust:dry-run` uploads nothing; the Cargo lane requires both policy and manifest publication guards to be explicitly enabled in an authorized release change.
`pmds catalog compile --target rust --schema <schema.pmd.json> --catalog-dir <dir>
--locale <tag> --output <dir>` compiles compatible PO updates without an application
build. Repeat `--locale` or `--fallback-locale` as needed; `--fail-on-missing`
opts into completeness checks, and `--json` emits output paths and fallback diagnostics.
Rust compilation defaults to build-time fallbacks; pmds UI builds explicitly opt into
strict completeness. Runtime load failures remain explicit and path-qualified.

Unbundled Node code (native type stripping, plain `tsc` output, scripts, tests)
can keep the `t`, `plural`, `select`, and `selectOrdinal` macros from
`@palamedes/core/macro`: `pmds extract --runtime-manifest .palamedes/macros.json`
records each call's static text, compiled key, and placeholder names, and
`pmds catalog compile --target js --output .palamedes/catalogs` writes one
parser-free `<locale>.mjs` per locale. Call `registerRuntimeMacros(url)` from
`@palamedes/runtime/node-macros` once at startup and `i18n.load(locale, messages)`
from the compiled module. Unregistered macros keep throwing; unknown calls and
missing catalogs throw instead of rendering source text. Runtime collisions and
interpolated choice branches are extraction errors. Bundled code compiles
macros with a plugin instead; Node load hooks, `tsc` preprocessing, and JSX
macros are unsupported here. `defineNodeI18n({ generated })` from
`@palamedes/runtime/node` wraps both steps, and server builds with
`@palamedes/vite-plugin` resolve it to the bundled catalog store, so one module
serves bundled and unbundled backends. See `docs/backend-servers.md`.

- `pmds report --fail-if-below 90`: per-locale completeness gate for CI
- Vue SFC scripts (Preview, browser-only): put `palamedes({ framework: "none", mdx: false })` before `@vitejs/plugin-vue`. Core macros work directly in inline `<script setup>` and `<script>` blocks, with native CLI extraction and automatic active-locale delivery. Setup-level calls execute per component; normal scripts retain function-scope rules. Template expressions/text and Vue rich text are not supported. See `/proof/vue-vite/README.md`. A separate private Nuxt 4 Node SSR proof verifies hydration, lazy routes, Nitro APIs, and concurrent request isolation in four languages; it targets root-mounted, same-origin query-locale deployment and is outside the supported example matrix. There is no published Nuxt package. See `/proof/nuxt-ssr/README.md`.
- Svelte component scripts (Preview, browser-only): put `palamedes({ framework: "none", mdx: false })` before `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`. Core macros work in inline JS/TS instance and module scripts, with native extraction, transforms, source maps, and automatic active-locale fragments. Instance-level calls execute per component; module scripts retain function-scope rules. Import macros in the script that uses them. Template expressions/text, Svelte rich text, and catalog HMR are outside the proof. See `/proof/svelte-vite/README.md`. A separate private SvelteKit 3 Node SSR proof verifies hydration, lazy components/routes, endpoint macros, parallel request isolation, and standalone output in four languages. It targets root-mounted, same-origin query-locale deployment with absolute asset paths and is outside the supported example matrix. There is no published SvelteKit package. See `/proof/sveltekit-ssr/README.md`.
- `pmds lint --json --fail-on warning`: non-mutating source-authoring diagnostics for configured JS, TS, JSX, TSX, MDX, Vue, and Svelte script blocks. Use `pmds lint` rather than the Preview ESLint/Oxlint adapter for stable CI and MDX.
- `pmds extract --check --json --fail-on-empty-catalog`: CI drift check with an empty-source guard. `--fail-on-empty-catalog` exits with code 1 before any configured catalog is written or marked obsolete when one catalog matches no source files. Without the flag, extraction warns and projects the empty catalog. Check JSON uses status `error`; watch mode leaves catalogs unchanged for the failed cycle and continues watching. The check can still update the extraction cache unless `--no-cache` is passed.
- Extraction-cache write failures are non-fatal but always warn on stderr, including for `pmds lint` and without `--verbose`; watch mode reports a persistent failure once per process rather than once per file event. Use `--no-cache` or `extract-cache: false` when the cache location is intentionally unwritable.
- `pmds catalog merge --conflict-strategy=use-first --output out.po a.po b.po`: semantic merge of exactly two catalogs; add `--base base.po` for a deletion-aware three-way merge. Supported PO/FCL extensions infer the format; use `--format po|fcl` only as an explicit override.
- `pmds catalog merge-driver %O %A %B %A --path %P --conflict-strategy=use-first`: one deletion-aware Git merge driver for PO and FCL. `%P` is the logical catalog path, so it selects the format even when Git temporary paths are extensionless; use `--format po|fcl` only as an explicit override. It maps merge and rebase roles so `use-first` stays the branch being merged or rebased.
- `pmds catalog convert --to fcl input.po`: convert PO catalogs to the opt-in FCL format

### CLI exit codes

| Code | CI meaning |
| ---- | ---------- |
| `0` | The command and its configured policy passed. |
| `1` | Configuration, I/O, serialization, or another operational failure. |
| `2` | Invalid command-line usage. |
| `3` | `extract --check` found catalog drift. |
| `4` | `lint` completed but its policy or source analysis failed. |
| `5` | `audit` completed but its `--fail-on` policy failed. |
| `6` | `report` completed but a locale was below `--fail-if-below`. |

## Lint adapters and translation automation APIs

`@palamedes/eslint-plugin` is a Preview ESLint/Oxlint facade over native source
diagnostics; `pmds lint` remains the stable CI and MDX interface. For custom
translation tooling, `@palamedes/core-node` exposes
`listTranslationCandidates(...)` and `applyTranslationPatches(...)`; create a
patch from the candidate `fingerprint` so stale catalog state is rejected.
Patches share audit's native ICU compatibility errors and allow compatible
target-language plural categories; a rejected batch leaves every catalog unchanged.
`inspectCatalogMachineTranslations(...)` (or its `Async` variant) reads PO/FCL
machine claims without rewriting files and exposes native current/stale/absent/invalid
statuses. These describe stored metadata integrity, not authorship or translation
quality; malformed metadata can be rejected or discarded before review.
File-touching custom integrations should use the additive `Async` catalog,
patch, compile, and extraction variants so native work runs on Node's shared
libuv worker pool instead of the event-loop thread; bound caller concurrency
because queued native work is not cancellable.

## CLI plugins

Third-party commands run as `pmds <plugin> <command>` and must be explicitly
listed under `plugins` in the Palamedes configuration — installed packages are
never auto-discovered. Plugins are binary-only native executables using the
versioned binary plugin protocol. Validated manifests are cached under
`.palamedes` and re-described when the binary, host, or protocol identity
changes; cache failures are non-fatal. See `/docs/cli.md` and
`/docs/api/cli-binary-plugin.md`.
